state.misconception_label: Believes if you changed all values by the same proportion the range would not change

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text:
I have: Tom and Katie are discussing the \( 5 \) plants with these heights: \( 24 \mathrm{~cm}, 17 \mathrm{~cm}, 42 \mathrm{~cm}, 26 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm} \) Tom says if all the plants were cut in half, the range wouldn't change. Katie says if all the plants grew by \( 3 \mathrm{~cm} \) each, the range wouldn't change. Who do you agree with? I got Only
Tom because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's clarify the concept of range. Remember, the range is the difference between the highest and lowest values in a set of data. Think about how cutting all the plants in half or growing them by the same amount would affect those values. Can you explain your reasoning behind choosing Tom?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I chose Tom because I thought if you cut all the heights in half, the highest and lowest would still be in the same proportion, so the range wouldn't change. But now I'm not sure if that’s right. Can you help me understand how the range changes when you add or cut values?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's work through an example to clarify this. If we cut all the plants' heights in half, what would be the new highest and lowest values? Then, calculate the range and see if it changes. This will help you better understand how changing values by the same proportion affects the range.

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Okay, so if we cut all the heights in half, the new heights would be \( 12 \mathrm{~cm}, 8.5 \mathrm{~cm}, 21 \mathrm{~cm}, 13 \mathrm{~cm}, \) and \( 6.5 \mathrm{~cm} \). The highest is \( 21 \mathrm{~cm} \) and the lowest is \( 6.5 \mathrm{~cm} \). So, the range would be \( 21 - 6.5 = 14.5 \mathrm{~cm} \). But I thought the range would stay the same because they are all just smaller. Does that mean I was wrong about Tom?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher effectively addresses the proportional change misconception by having the student calculate concrete values, leading to visible cognitive progress when the student discovers the range does change (14.5 vs original 29) and questions their initial reasoning.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses primarily Socratic questioning and guided discovery rather than direct explanation with worked examples, which is inconsistent with the traditional strategy of explaining concepts directly.
